title: Journey of Swami Vivekananda
coverageNote: A sourced atlas of principal documented journeys and life events, with selected residences, lecture venues and transit stops. It is not an exhaustive diary of every day or every local excursion. No marker is added for an intended trip that was not completed.

goa.title: Swami Vivekananda’s visit to Goa
goa.note: Records the October 1892 stay at Margao, Subrai Naik’s hospitality, the Rachol Seminary visit and temple visits. Exact days for individual excursions are not supplied.

goa-arrival.title: History of a Goa Ashrama: origins
goa-arrival.note: Dates the arrival at Margao to 27 October 1892.

ew.title: The Life of Swami Vivekananda by His Eastern and Western Disciples
ew.publisher: Advaita Ashrama, Ramakrishna Math; official Ramakrishna Order online reader
ew.note: The official online edition is linked here. Individual chapter citations also link the 1960-edition transcription hosted by the Order’s Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute. Devotional experiences are presented as the biographers’ accounts.

belur.title: Swami Vivekananda: life and contributions
belur.publisher: Belur Math, Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission
belur.note: Preferred official account for principal life events and disagreements. Specific Belur Math site histories supply finer dates where available; unspecified dates are not filled in.

west.title: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology
west.publisher: Terrance Hohner and Carolyn Kenny, Vedanta Society of Portland; hosted by Vedanta Society of Southern California
west.note: A day-by-day record for July 1893–December 1900, citing the Complete Works, the Life, Marie Louise Burke’s New Discoveries, and later research. Entries marked “probably” or “?” are not treated as certain.

letter.title: Letter III to Alasinga and friends, Yokohama, 10 July 1893
letter.note: Swamiji’s own account of Colombo, Penang, Singapore, Hong Kong, Canton, Nagasaki, Kobe, Osaka, Kyoto, Tokyo, and Yokohama.

chicago.title: Addresses at the Parliament of Religions
chicago.note: The dated address of 11 September 1893. Other Parliament addresses are linked from the volume.

oldmath.title: Old Math: Nilambar Babu’s Garden House
oldmath.note: History of the temporary monastery and Swamiji’s work there.

room.title: Swamiji’s Room
room.note: Swamiji’s room and the preservation of his belongings at Belur Math.

hyderabad.title: Commemoration of Swami Vivekananda’s visit to Hyderabad
hyderabad.publisher: Belur Math Media Gallery / Ramakrishna Math, Hyderabad
hyderabad.note: Confirms the lecture “My Mission to the West” at Mahboob College on 13 February 1893.

canada.title: Swami Vivekananda in Canada
canada.note: Used alongside the Western chronology for the Pacific crossing and Canadian transit.

belur-videos.title: Kanyakumari meditation: official documentary listing
belur-videos.publisher: Belur Math; documentary by Sri Ramakrishna Math, Chennai
belur-videos.note: Belur Math lists the Kanyakumari meditation as 24–26 December 1892. The atlas follows this published official dating.

belur-belagavi.title: Swami Vivekananda in Belagavi: memorial history
belur-belagavi.note: Dates the Belagavi stay to 16–27 October 1892, including 16–18 October with the Bhate family.

belur-150-sites.title: Vivek Ganga Parikrama: histories of associated sites
belur-150-sites.publisher: Belur Math, official 150th birth anniversary website
belur-150-sites.note: Provides the Shyampukur residence period, Old Math’s opening period, Kalighat association and the 1899 embarkation site. Residence dates do not imply Swamiji attended every day.

belur-kakrighat.title: Kakrighat: the sacred Peepal tree and Swamiji’s visit
belur-kakrighat.note: Identifies Kakrighat and the meditation under the Peepal tree in 1890. It gives no calendar day.

belur-akhandananda.title: Swami Akhandananda: the Himalayan journey and Meerut
belur-akhandananda.note: Documents the interrupted Himalayan pilgrimage, recovery and reunion at Meerut. It does not establish exact Meerut arrival and departure days.

belur-places.title: Places to see at Belur Math: old shrine, present temple and Swamiji’s room
belur-places.note: Distinguishes the old shrine from the present Sri Ramakrishna temple, consecrated on 14 January 1938. It records Swamiji’s Mahasamadhi in his room on 4 July 1902.

official-works.title: The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda: official online edition
official-works.publisher: Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission publications portal
official-works.note: Official reading access to Swamiji’s letters, lectures and writings. Individual event references retain their specific volume, dated letter or address and a direct transcription link.

journeys.name: Roots & awakening
journeys.description: Narendranath’s family, education, apprenticeship with Sri Ramakrishna, and the first monastic brotherhood.

journeys.name: The wandering monk · North
journeys.description: Early pilgrimages and the Himalayan journey. Several dates survive only as periods; intended visits to Kedarnath and Badrinath are not mapped as completed visits.

journeys.name: Across western & southern India
journeys.description: Rajputana, Gujarat, Maharashtra and the south. A selection of confirmed stops; broad date ranges deliberately preserve uncertainty in the early itinerary.

journeys.name: To Chicago · the first crossing
journeys.description: His July letter records the Asian stops; later research documents the Pacific arrival and the Canadian rail journey.

journeys.name: Teaching in America & Europe
journeys.description: Public lectures, small classes, friendships and Vedanta work across the United States, Britain and continental Europe.

journeys.name: The homecoming
journeys.description: The voyage from Naples, reception in Ceylon and southern India, and return to Calcutta.

journeys.name: Service, disciples & the Math
journeys.description: The Mission, northern lecture tour, training of disciples, Kashmir pilgrimage, and the establishment of Belur Math.

journeys.name: The second Western journey
journeys.description: The Golconda voyage, Ridgely, California, Paris and the Mediterranean journey home.

journeys.name: The final years
journeys.description: Mayavati, pilgrimage with his mother, the last visits to Bodh Gaya and Varanasi, and life at Belur Math.

events.title: Birth of Narendranath Datta
events.description: Narendranath was born in the Datta family in Calcutta. His parents were Vishwanath Datta, an attorney, and Bhuvaneshwari Devi.
events.significance: His mother’s devotional storytelling and his father’s broad interests shaped his early world.

events.title: School years
events.description: Narendra entered Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar’s Metropolitan Institution. He combined study with music, exercise, games and an interest in public life.
events.significance: His education brought Indian learning and modern subjects into the same life.

events.title: Two years in Raipur
events.description: The family moved to Raipur while his father worked there. Narendra spent time learning from his father and discussing a wide range of subjects.
events.significance: The stay interrupted regular schooling but broadened his intellectual education.
events.uncertainty: The biography dates the move to 1877. No exact arrival or departure day is established here.

events.title: Return to Calcutta
events.description: Back in Calcutta, Narendra resumed school and passed the entrance examination.
events.significance: This prepared him for college study.

events.title: At Presidency College
events.description: Narendra enrolled at Presidency College before continuing at the General Assembly’s Institution.
events.significance: He encountered the curriculum of a modern college in colonial Calcutta.

events.title: Philosophy, music and a spiritual search
events.description: At the General Assembly’s Institution he studied Western philosophy and other subjects. Principal William Hastie referred him to Sri Ramakrishna when discussing spiritual experience.
events.significance: His question about direct knowledge of God became central to his search.

events.title: An early meeting with Sri Ramakrishna
events.description: The disciples’ biography places an early encounter at Surendra Nath Mitra’s home, where Narendra sang before Sri Ramakrishna.
events.significance: It began a relationship that would redirect his life.
events.uncertainty: The house encounter is recorded in the Order’s fuller biography. Belur Math’s overview dates the Dakshineswar meeting to November 1881; that official dating is used for the separate Dakshineswar event. The accounts describe the opening encounters differently; no exact day or precise interval between them is asserted.

sources.locator: With Sri Ramakrishna: November 1881 Dakshineswar account, compared with the fuller Order biography

events.title: At the feet of Sri Ramakrishna
events.description: Narendra visited Sri Ramakrishna at Dakshineswar. Over repeated visits he questioned, tested and gradually accepted the teacher whose spiritual experience he sought to understand.
events.significance: Dakshineswar became the principal setting of his spiritual training.
events.uncertainty: The displayed month follows Belur Math’s official “With Sri Ramakrishna” account. The fuller Order biography narrates an earlier house encounter separately. No exact day is given in the official overview.

sources.locator: With Sri Ramakrishna: visit to Dakshineswar in November 1881

events.title: Graduation and family hardship
events.description: Narendra completed his B.A. His father’s sudden death that year left the family in severe financial difficulty; he tried to find work while continuing his spiritual search.
events.significance: Personal hardship deepened his encounter with poverty and responsibility.

events.title: Prayer at the Kali temple
events.description: The biography recounts that, urged by Sri Ramakrishna to seek help for his family, Narendra prayed instead for spiritual knowledge and devotion.
events.significance: The episode is important in the Order’s account of his acceptance of the Divine Mother.
events.uncertainty: A devotional episode recorded by the biographers; the precise day is not established.

events.title: Nursing the Master
events.description: When Sri Ramakrishna’s throat illness required treatment in Calcutta, Narendra joined the young disciples caring for him at Shyampukur.
events.significance: Shared service strengthened the group that would become the monastic brotherhood.
events.uncertainty: These are Sri Ramakrishna’s residence dates, given in Belur Math’s official site history; they frame Narendra’s care for him and do not imply continuous daily attendance. The specific site history is used rather than the overview’s broader September wording.

events.title: Cossipore: service and spiritual training
events.description: At the garden house the disciples nursed Sri Ramakrishna while practising meditation and study. Narendra increasingly took responsibility for the group.
events.significance: The future Order took shape in this close circle of service.

events.title: A pilgrimage to Buddha Gaya
events.description: Narendra went to Buddha Gaya with Tarak and Kali, later Swamis Shivananda and Abhedananda, and meditated at the place associated with the Buddha’s enlightenment.
events.significance: His reverence for the Buddha remained a lasting feature of his thought.

events.title: Sri Ramakrishna’s passing
events.description: Sri Ramakrishna passed away at Cossipore. Narendra and the other disciples now faced the task of sustaining their shared spiritual life.
events.significance: This marked the transition from discipleship around a living teacher to the organisation of a brotherhood.

events.title: The first monastery
events.description: The disciples gathered at a rented house in Baranagar, supported by Surendranath Mitra. Narendra encouraged meditation, scriptural study and wide intellectual discussion.
events.significance: Baranagar was the first home of the Ramakrishna monastic brotherhood.
events.people: Surendranath Mitra; Shashi and the brother disciples

events.title: A vow of renunciation at Antpur
events.description: At Baburam’s family home, the disciples gathered around a fire. Narendra spoke about the life of Jesus, and they resolved to dedicate themselves to monastic life.
events.significance: This shared commitment is remembered as a formative moment of the Order.
events.people: Baburam, later Swami Premananda; the brother disciples

events.title: Formal monastic vows
events.description: The young disciples performed the Viraja ceremony and took formal vows of renunciation at Baranagar. Narendra used several monastic names before “Vivekananda” became established.
events.significance: The informal brotherhood became a community of vowed monks.
events.uncertainty: Belur Math dates the formal vows to 1887 and explicitly notes that the name Vivekananda was assumed later. The fuller biography supplies the early-year period; no single naming day is asserted.

sources.locator: Beginnings of a Monastic Brotherhood: vows in 1887; the name Vivekananda came later

events.title: The first northern pilgrimages
events.description: He visited Varanasi, its temples and ascetics, including Trailanga Swami and Bhaskarananda.
events.significance: The holy city was an early school of pilgrimage, debate and independent monastic life.

events.title: Friendship with Pramadadas Mitra
events.description: On another visit he met the Sanskrit scholar Pramadadas Mitra. Their later correspondence dealt with scripture and social questions.
events.significance: The friendship supported his studies during years of wandering.
events.uncertainty: A separate visit is described; exact days for the early Varanasi trips are not established.

events.title: In the city of Rama
events.description: He visited Ayodhya, listening to devotional singing and reflecting on the Ramayana.
events.significance: These visits widened his understanding of India’s religious and artistic inheritance.

events.title: The heritage of Lucknow
events.description: He saw the palaces, gardens and mosques associated with the Nawabs of Oudh.
events.significance: These visits widened his understanding of India’s religious and artistic inheritance.

events.title: At the Taj Mahal
events.description: The biography records repeated visits to the Taj Mahal and admiration for its workmanship.
events.significance: These visits widened his understanding of India’s religious and artistic inheritance.

events.title: Pilgrimage to Vrindaban
events.description: He reached Vrindaban on foot during his northern travels. The biography recounts an encounter with a roadside smoker that made him confront his own inherited caste reflexes.
events.significance: The episode connects his teaching of spiritual equality with self-examination.

events.title: A disciple at Hathras
events.description: At Hathras railway station he met station-master Sharat Chandra Gupta, who became his disciple and later Swami Sadananda.
events.significance: One of his earliest disciples was drawn to the ideal of serving India.
events.people: Sharat Chandra Gupta, later Swami Sadananda

events.title: Towards the Himalayan foothills
events.description: He travelled with Sharat Chandra Gupta through Hardwar towards Hrishikesh.
events.significance: The journey brought teacher and disciple into the life of wandering ascetics.

events.title: Meditation and illness
events.description: He and his new disciple practised at Hrishikesh. Illness interrupted their stay and led them back towards Hathras and Baranagar.
events.significance: The hardships of pilgrimage were part of his early monastic experience.

events.title: At Vaidyanath
events.description: During another northern journey he stayed at Vaidyanath. News that Swami Yogananda was ill prompted him to go to Allahabad.
events.significance: Care for his brother disciples repeatedly changed his travel plans.

events.title: Nursing Yogananda
events.description: He went to Allahabad to care for Swami Yogananda and met local residents and a Muslim saint.
events.significance: His wandering life combined solitude, religious encounter and personal service.

events.title: Pavhari Baba at Ghazipur
events.description: He stayed with friends and visited the ascetic Pavhari Baba. Letters from this period document physical pain and an intense spiritual struggle.
events.significance: This was a significant period of reflection on his loyalty to Sri Ramakrishna and the place of yoga in his life.
events.people: Pavhari Baba; Satish Chandra Mukherjee; Gagan Chandra Roy

events.title: Back to Benares
events.description: He returned to Varanasi, attended to Swami Abhedananda’s illness and stayed with Pramadadas Mitra.
events.significance: The return joins scholarly friendship with care for a brother monk.

events.title: Holy Mother’s blessing
events.description: Before setting out again, he received the blessings of Sri Sarada Devi. He left with Swami Akhandananda for a longer journey through northern India.
events.significance: The departure began the sustained wandering that preceded his public mission.

events.title: Learning and music at Bhagalpur
events.description: He stayed with Manmatha Nath Chowdhury and conversed about the Upanishads, yoga and religion; his singing also impressed his hosts.
events.significance: Private conversations were an important form of teaching before his public lectures.

events.title: Meeting Raj Narayan Bose
events.description: At Vaidyanath, he and Akhandananda met the Brahmo thinker Raj Narayan Bose.
events.significance: The encounter linked the wandering monk with an older generation of Indian religious reform.

events.title: A brief halt in Varanasi
events.description: He again stayed with Pramadadas Mitra before travelling towards the Himalayas.
events.significance: This was another distinct visit to a recurring centre of his life.

events.title: A scholar-ascetic in Ayodhya
events.description: He visited the ashrama of Janakivar Saran with Akhandananda.
events.significance: He valued learning combined with spiritual practice.

events.title: Naini Tal on the Himalayan journey
events.description: The two monks stayed with Ram Prasanna Bhattacharya before walking towards Almora.
events.significance: Their onward journey was undertaken with little money and a resolve to travel simply.

events.title: Meditation near Almora
events.description: Near a stream and peepul tree on the way to Almora, the biography records a meditation followed by reflections on the microcosm and macrocosm.
events.significance: The experience is important in the biographical account of his sense of the unity of existence.
events.uncertainty: Belur Math’s official account identifies Kakrighat and the year 1890. It does not give a month or day. The spiritual realisation is presented as the Order’s biographical account.

sources.locator: Opening historical account: meditation at Kakrighat in 1890

events.title: Brother monks in Almora
events.description: He met fellow disciples and stayed with Lala Badri Shah before continuing into Garhwal.
events.significance: Almora became a place to which he would return on later journeys.
events.people: Lala Badri Shah; Swami Saradananda; Swami Akhandananda

events.title: An interrupted pilgrimage
events.description: The party reached Karnaprayag, but the route towards Kedarnath and Badrinath was closed during famine. They did not complete those intended pilgrimages.
events.significance: The Himalayan itinerary was shaped by illness, companionship and changing conditions.

sources.locator: As a Wandering Monk: interrupted pilgrimage via Almora, Karnaprayag, Tehri, Dehradun and Rishikesh

events.title: Study by the Alakananda
events.description: The monks stayed in a hut at Srinagar in Garhwal and studied the Upanishads together.
events.significance: The Himalayan itinerary was shaped by illness, companionship and changing conditions.

events.title: A stay at Tehri
events.description: He and his companions lived near the Ganga and considered arrangements for secluded practice.
events.significance: The Himalayan itinerary was shaped by illness, companionship and changing conditions.

events.title: Care for Akhandananda
events.description: They moved to Dehra Dun as Akhandananda needed medical attention.
events.significance: The Himalayan itinerary was shaped by illness, companionship and changing conditions.

sources.locator: As a Wandering Monk: interrupted pilgrimage via Almora, Karnaprayag, Tehri, Dehradun and Rishikesh

events.title: A second stay at Hrishikesh
events.description: He stayed with brother monks near Chandeshwar Mahadeva. Severe illness interrupted his spiritual practices.
events.significance: The Himalayan itinerary was shaped by illness, companionship and changing conditions.

sources.locator: As a Wandering Monk: interrupted pilgrimage via Almora, Karnaprayag, Tehri, Dehradun and Rishikesh

events.title: Convalescence at Hardwar
events.description: After the illness at Hrishikesh, the monks brought him to Hardwar before moving on to Meerut.
events.significance: The Himalayan itinerary was shaped by illness, companionship and changing conditions.

events.title: A brotherhood reunited in Meerut
events.description: In a garden at Meerut, he and several brother monks read, meditated and sang together. He also borrowed books from the local library.
events.significance: This temporary community recalled Baranagar before he chose to travel alone.
events.uncertainty: Belur Math’s Akhandananda biography describes five months of association with the brother monks, while the fuller biography also mentions a roughly five-month Meerut stay. Exact arrival and departure dates are not established here; the broad 1890–1891 period avoids turning these recollections into invented calendar days.

sources.locator: As a Wandering Monk: illness, reunion at Meerut and subsequent separation

events.title: Setting out alone
events.description: He left the brother monks and went to Delhi under the name Vividishananda, visiting monuments of earlier empires.
events.significance: He sought the freedom of travelling without old attachments.

events.title: Religious discussion in Alwar
events.description: He met people of different faiths and Maharaja Mangal Singh. The biography recounts his explanation of image worship through a portrait of the ruler.
events.significance: He defended religious symbols while inviting practical effort and learning.
events.people: Maharaja Mangal Singh; Major Ramchandra; Guru Charan Laskar

events.title: A halt at Pandupol
events.description: Leaving Alwar with companions, he travelled by bullock cart and slept in the Hanuman temple compound at Pandupol.
events.significance: A documented village and temple halt reveals the smaller stages within his travels.

events.title: Sanskrit study at Jaipur
events.description: He studied grammar and stayed with admirers in Jaipur. A photograph of him as a wandering monk was taken during this visit.
events.significance: Study and conversation accompanied his travels through Rajputana.

events.title: Ajmer’s historical inheritance
events.description: He visited Ajmer before going on to Mount Abu.
events.significance: The city’s Hindu and Muslim history formed part of his encounter with India’s composite culture.

events.title: Meeting Ajit Singh
events.description: At Mount Abu he met Maharaja Ajit Singh of Khetri after staying with a Muslim host.
events.significance: This began a friendship that provided important personal and practical support for his mission.
events.people: Maharaja Ajit Singh; Munshi Jagmohan Lal

events.title: At the court of Khetri
events.description: He stayed with Ajit Singh, discussing spiritual subjects and the responsibilities of life.
events.significance: Khetri became one of his enduring relationships with an Indian ruler.

events.title: Ahmedabad: history and religion
events.description: He stayed with Lal Shankar Umia Shankar and explored Hindu, Jain and Islamic learning and monuments.
events.significance: He encountered Gujarat’s varied religious traditions.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Through Wadhwan
events.description: The disciples’ biography names Wadhwan as a stop before Limbdi.
events.significance: It preserves a smaller stage in his western Indian itinerary.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: The Thakore of Limbdi
events.description: The ruler of Limbdi became an admirer and helped him with introductions.
events.significance: Personal networks enabled a penniless monk to meet scholars and officials.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Through Bhavnagar
events.description: He visited Bhavnagar and Sihor on the way to Junagad with recommendations from Limbdi.
events.significance: These were documented stages in his travels through Kathiawar.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Junagad and Mount Girnar
events.description: He stayed with Dewan Haridas Viharidas and visited historic and sacred sites, including Girnar.
events.significance: He discussed religion, education and public welfare with the Dewan and other residents.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: In Cutch
events.description: He stayed with the Dewan at Bhooj and conversed with the Maharaja of Cutch.
events.significance: His discussions with rulers included the possibility of improving conditions for their people.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: At Somnath and Prabhas
events.description: He visited the Somnath temples and the confluence of rivers at Prabhas.
events.significance: The site prompted reflection on India’s history and spiritual endurance.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Study at Porbandar
events.description: He worked with the scholar-administrator Shankar Pandurang, studying Sanskrit and discussing the Vedas.
events.significance: His host encouraged him to carry his ideas to the West.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Pilgrimage to Dwaraka
events.description: He visited the sacred coastal town of Dwaraka during his Gujarat travels.
events.significance: Pilgrimage and reflection were part of his preparation for a wider mission.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: A meeting at Mandvi
events.description: He met Swami Akhandananda at Mandvi after his brother monk had searched for him.
events.significance: Even while seeking solitude, he remained connected to the brotherhood.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Narayan Sarovar
events.description: The biography records a journey to Narayan Sarovar and Ashapuri before his return to Mandvi.
events.significance: The western pilgrimage included remote sacred places as well as princely capitals.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: The hill of Shatrunjaya
events.description: He visited Palitana and ascended the sacred hill of Shatrunjaya.
events.significance: The itinerary included important Jain pilgrimage centres.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: A short stay in Baroda
events.description: He stayed with Dewan Manibhai in Baroda before moving towards central India.
events.significance: The stop continued his conversations with administrators and thinkers.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: Considering the Parliament
events.description: At Khandwa he stayed with Haridas Chatterjee and spoke of attending the forthcoming Parliament of Religions in Chicago.
events.significance: The idea of travelling to the West was becoming a practical possibility.
events.uncertainty: The visit is documented; the precise date within the western Indian tour is not fixed here. The order of all side trips is not certain.

events.title: A first stay in Bombay
events.description: He stayed with Chhabildas in Bombay and discussed contemporary social issues.
events.significance: The port city later became the starting point of his first overseas voyage.

events.title: With Bal Gangadhar Tilak
events.description: He stayed in Poona with Bal Gangadhar Tilak and discussed religion and other subjects.
events.significance: The visit brought him into contact with an important scholar and public figure.

events.title: The Limbdi ruler at Mahabaleshwar
events.description: He visited the Thakore of Limbdi, who was staying at Mahabaleshwar.
events.significance: The encounter renewed a friendship formed in Gujarat.

events.title: At Kolhapur
events.description: He visited the princely court and received an introduction that helped his onward journey to Belgaum.
events.significance: Support from hosts enabled the next stage of his travels.

events.title: Conversations at Belgaum
events.description: He stayed with the Bhate family and then Haripada Mitra. Mitra’s diary records meeting him on 18 October and discussions of religion, literature and daily responsibility.
events.significance: The recollections preserve his humour, learning and concern for public health and poverty.
events.uncertainty: The stay dates follow Belur Math’s official memorial history. The first three days, 16–18 October, were spent with the Bhate family.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in Belagavi: 12-day stay and Bhate house

events.title: Arriving in Margao
events.description: The Ramakrishna Mission’s local history dates his arrival in Margao to this day. Sanskrit scholar Subrai Naik hosted him.
events.significance: Goa became a setting for his study of Christian traditions alongside Hindu devotional life.

sources.locator: History of a Goa Ashrama: origins

events.title: Studying at Rachol Seminary
events.description: The Mission’s local account records a three-day visit to study Christian theology at the seminary, facilitated by Subrai Naik.
events.significance: The visit broadens the record of his engagement with religions during his Indian travels.
events.uncertainty: The source records three days but does not establish their calendar dates here.

events.significance: These visits place local Hindu religious life alongside his study of Christianity.

events.title: Bangalore and the Mysore State
events.description: He stayed in Bangalore and came into contact with the Mysore State’s Dewan, K. Seshadri Iyer.
events.significance: The connections led to significant discussions at the Mysore court.

events.title: At the Mysore court
events.description: He met Maharaja Chamarajendra Wadiyar and addressed scholars on Vedanta. He described India’s need for scientific knowledge alongside its spiritual inheritance.
events.significance: The court offered support for his proposed journey to America.
events.people: Maharaja Chamarajendra Wadiyar; K. Seshadri Iyer

events.title: Through Trichur
events.description: He travelled from Mysore into Kerala, with Trichur named as a stop in the biography.
events.significance: The southward journey continued towards Travancore and the tip of India.

events.title: A guest in Trivandrum
events.description: He stayed with Professor Sundararama Iyer and met scholars and officials, including Prince Martanda Varma.
events.significance: His hosts recalled discussions ranging from religion and philosophy to science and India’s social condition.
events.people: Sundararama Iyer; Professor Rangacharya; Prince Martanda Varma

events.title: Meeting the Raja of Ramnad
events.description: He met Bhaskara Setupati, the Raja of Ramnad, and discussed education and the condition of the masses.
events.significance: The Raja urged him to attend the Parliament and promised help.
events.uncertainty: Biographical accounts arrange Madurai, Rameswaram and Kanyakumari differently. These visits are retained with broad dates; no exact sequence is claimed.

events.title: Pilgrimage to Rameswaram
events.description: He worshipped at Rameswaram, fulfilling a cherished intention during his travels in southern India.
events.significance: The visit joined his life of pilgrimage with the emerging plan to go abroad.
events.uncertainty: The order relative to Kanyakumari differs between biographical narratives.

events.title: Meditation at India’s southern tip
events.description: At Kanyakumari he meditated on a rock offshore and reflected on India’s past, poverty and possibilities for renewal.
events.significance: The episode is remembered as a turning point towards an active mission of service and education.
events.uncertainty: The date range follows the official Kanyakumari documentary listing on Belur Math’s website. This is the published official dating; it does not establish an exact road or sea route to the rock.

sources.locator: Video listing: meditation on Mother India at Kanyakumari, 24–26 December 1892

events.title: Through Pondicherry
events.description: The biography names Pondicherry among the stops on his journey towards Madras.
events.significance: His south Indian network grew before the first overseas journey.

events.title: The Madras circle
events.description: At Madras he met enthusiastic young supporters led by Alasinga Perumal. They discussed his proposed Western mission and raised money from supporters.
events.significance: The Madras disciples became essential collaborators in his later work.
events.people: Alasinga Perumal; M. C. Nanjunda Rao; other Madras disciples

events.title: “My Mission to the West”
events.description: He gave a public lecture at Mahboob College in Secunderabad during his Hyderabad visit.
events.significance: The address was an early public statement of the mission he intended to undertake.

sources.locator: Commemoration of Swami Vivekananda’s visit to Hyderabad

events.title: Khetri before departure
events.description: He returned at Ajit Singh’s invitation after the birth of a royal son. The ruler helped with the arrangements for his journey abroad.
events.significance: The name “Vivekananda” became established around this departure period.
events.people: Maharaja Ajit Singh; Munshi Jagmohan Lal
events.uncertainty: Belur Math notes that the name Vivekananda was assumed later than the 1887 vows. Its overview confirms Khetri’s support for the Western journey but does not date the naming to a particular day; the departure period is retained from the fuller Order biography.

sources.locator: Decision to attend the Parliament: Khetri patronage; the overview does not supply a naming day

events.title: A farewell at Abu Road
events.description: On the way to Bombay he met Swamis Brahmananda and Turiyananda at Abu Road railway station.
events.significance: The remembered conversation linked his journey to America with the suffering he had seen in India.

events.title: Departure for the West
events.description: He sailed from Bombay aboard the Peninsular, beginning the journey that would take him to Chicago.
events.significance: Support from Indian friends and patrons made the overseas mission possible.

events.significance: The stay forms part of the interval between institutional work and the second Western journey.

events.title: Preparing a second Western mission
events.description: He trained monks and disciples while preparing to visit the work in the West again.
events.significance: He intended to strengthen the centres already started abroad.

events.title: Sailing on the Golconda
events.description: He left Calcutta for the West with Swami Turiyananda and Sister Nivedita.
events.significance: The second visit aimed to sustain and expand Vedanta work.

sources.locator: Site 4, Princep Ghat: boarding the Golconda on 20 June 1899

events.title: Madras: a harbour call
events.description: The Golconda called at Madras, but passengers coming from plague-affected Calcutta were not allowed to land. Friends met the ship from boats.
events.significance: A port call must not be mistaken for another stay ashore.
events.uncertainty: Transit only: Swamiji did not disembark during this call.

events.title: Colombo again
events.description: The voyage continued through Colombo.
events.significance: This entry records the port sequence; it does not claim an undocumented excursion ashore.
events.uncertainty: Port call or transit. Exact time ashore is not established.

events.title: A port call at Aden
events.description: Aden is named among the Golconda’s documented calls.
events.significance: This entry records the port sequence; it does not claim an undocumented excursion ashore.
events.uncertainty: Port call or transit. Exact time ashore is not established.

events.title: Naples on the voyage
events.description: The steamer called at Naples while he remained subject to the voyage’s health restrictions.
events.significance: This entry records the port sequence; it does not claim an undocumented excursion ashore.
events.uncertainty: Port call or transit. Exact time ashore is not established.

events.title: Through Marseilles
events.description: Marseilles was a further documented call on the way to Britain.
events.significance: This entry records the port sequence; it does not claim an undocumented excursion ashore.
events.uncertainty: Port call or transit. Exact time ashore is not established.

events.title: Arrival in England
events.description: He arrived in England and spent time in the London area with friends and disciples.
events.significance: The stay preceded his return to the United States.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: The Atlantic departure
events.description: He travelled to Glasgow and sailed for America on the Numidian.
events.significance: The Scottish port began the Atlantic leg of the second journey.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Back in America
events.description: He arrived in the New York region, with friends meeting the returning party.
events.significance: The visit began with time away from the pressure of public work.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: A long stay at Ridgely
events.description: The Leggett family hosted him at Ridgely Manor. He rested, taught informally and spent time with Western disciples and friends.
events.significance: The stay was a major restorative interval in his later life.
events.people: Francis and Betty Leggett; Josephine MacLeod; Sister Nivedita; Swami Turiyananda

events.title: New York before California
events.description: He visited friends and the Vedanta Society before leaving for the western United States.
events.significance: He reviewed the American work and prepared another period of teaching.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Old friends in Chicago
events.description: He broke the transcontinental journey to see the Hale family and other friends.
events.significance: The visit renewed relationships dating to his first American arrival.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Teaching in Los Angeles
events.description: He arrived in Los Angeles and stayed first with Miss Spencer, then with Mrs. Blodgett, giving lectures and classes.
events.significance: The California work opened a new centre of activity on America’s Pacific coast.
events.people: Josephine MacLeod; Mrs. S. K. Blodgett; Miss Spencer

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: “Christ, the Messenger”
events.description: He gave the lecture “Christ, the Messenger” at the Universalist Church in Pasadena.
events.significance: The address expressed his reverence for Jesus within a universal view of spiritual life.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: The Mead sisters’ home
events.description: He stayed with the Mead sisters in South Pasadena while teaching in the Los Angeles area.
events.significance: Their recollections preserve a close view of his everyday life and work.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Classes in Pasadena
events.description: He gave a series of talks at the Shakespeare Club and other venues, on yoga and Indian religious subjects.
events.significance: Small classes and public talks helped build a local circle of students.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Lectures in Oakland
events.description: Invited by Rev. Benjamin Fay Mills, he spoke at the First Unitarian Church and addressed large audiences.
events.significance: These meetings were a principal beginning of his work around San Francisco Bay.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Vedanta in San Francisco
events.description: He lectured, gave classes and worked with students in San Francisco. The Vedanta Society was founded during this period.
events.significance: The work established a lasting institutional presence on the West Coast.
events.people: Dr. Milburn Logan; Alice Hansbrough; other students

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Reflection at Alameda
events.description: He stayed with the Home of Truth circle. His letter to Josephine MacLeod dated 18 April expresses a deeply reflective mood.
events.significance: The letter offers a firsthand view of his inner life during this final American period.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Camp life in Marin County
events.description: He stayed with a small group at Camp Taylor, teaching, meditating and cooking with them.
events.significance: The retreat joined everyday companionship with informal spiritual teaching.
events.people: Alice Hansbrough; members of the camp party

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Farewell to California
events.description: He returned to the Bay Area before leaving for the eastern United States.
events.significance: The final California meetings handed continuing work to local students.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: The last Chicago visit
events.description: He stayed with the Hale family on his way east.
events.significance: This was his last meeting with some of the friends who had supported him since 1893.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: A final visit to Detroit
events.description: He stopped in Detroit during the return journey to New York.
events.significance: The stop renewed another circle of American friendships.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Final New York classes
events.description: He lectured at the Vedanta Society and discussed plans for Turiyananda’s California work.
events.significance: The American centres would continue through his brother disciples and students.

events.title: Paris and the Exposition
events.description: He attended the Paris Exposition and the Congress of the History of Religions, meeting scholars, artists and friends.
events.significance: The 1900 congress was a historical scholarly gathering, distinct from the 1893 Parliament.
events.people: Jules Bois; Emma Calvé; Josephine MacLeod; Jagadish Chandra Bose

events.title: The Congress of the History of Religions
events.description: He spoke at the congress about Indian religious history and challenged interpretations of Hindu symbols.
events.significance: His contribution applied historical argument to the study of religion.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: A brief stay in Brittany
events.description: He visited friends in the Lannion and Brittany coastal area before returning to Paris.
events.significance: A quieter stay interrupted the busy Exposition season.
events.uncertainty: Accounts name Lannion and nearby Perros-Guirec. The marker covers the locality rather than a verified house.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: At Mont Saint-Michel
events.description: The Western chronology records a visit to Mont Saint-Michel on the feast of the Archangel Michael.
events.significance: The visit belongs to his interest in the religious architecture of Europe.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Returning to Paris
events.description: The Western chronology records his return from the Brittany and Normandy visit to Paris.
events.significance: This separates the first coastal visit from a further October stay.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: A second Brittany stay
events.description: The Western chronology records another stay at Perros-Guirec in October, with Jules Bois and Josephine MacLeod.
events.significance: The separate entry preserves a repeat visit during his final European journey.
events.uncertainty: The chronology questions the lodging attribution; no exact house or host arrangement is asserted.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Paris before the journey east
events.description: He returned to Paris before leaving by train for Vienna on 24 October.
events.significance: Paris was the departure point for the overland and Mediterranean journey home.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Vienna on the journey east
events.description: Travelling with Emma Calvé, Josephine MacLeod and Jules Bois, he visited Vienna and its museums and palace.
events.significance: The journey combined historical sightseeing with conversations among friends.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Constantinople and the Bosporus
events.description: He visited Constantinople, crossed the Bosporus and spoke to small audiences.
events.significance: The city added another setting for his engagement with religious and cultural traditions.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: The monuments of Athens
events.description: He visited the Acropolis and other ancient sites before sailing for Egypt.
events.significance: The journey brought him into direct contact with Greek historical remains.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Cairo and the journey home
events.description: He visited Egypt with his companions, including the pyramids and Sphinx, then decided to return to India.
events.significance: The Egyptian stay was the last stage of his travels outside India.

sources.locator: Swami Vivekananda in the West: A Chronology

events.title: Back on Indian soil
events.description: He disembarked at Bombay and continued by train towards Calcutta.
events.significance: This completed his second Western journey.

events.title: An unannounced homecoming
events.description: He returned to Belur Math in the evening without advance notice to the monks.
events.significance: He was again among the brotherhood after the long second Western tour.

events.title: Towards Mayavati
events.description: He reached the railhead at Kathgodam and continued into the hills during severe winter weather.
events.significance: The visit was prompted by Captain Sevier’s death and concern for Charlotte Sevier.

events.title: At Advaita Ashrama
events.description: He visited Charlotte Sevier and the community at Mayavati, wrote essays and discussed the ashrama’s commitment to non-dualistic study and practice.
events.significance: This was his visit to the Himalayan centre founded under his inspiration.
events.people: Charlotte Sevier; Swami Swarupananda; Swami Virajananda

events.title: The return through Pilibhit
events.description: Returning from Mayavati via Tanakpur, he reached Pilibhit and continued by rail.
events.significance: The biography documents this smaller transit stage of the winter journey.

events.title: Home from Mayavati
events.description: He arrived back at Belur Math and resumed guiding the monastery’s work.
events.significance: The stay preceded a final public tour with a personal pilgrimage purpose.

events.title: A river-and-rail arrival
events.description: He came by steamer from Goalando to Narayanganj and then by train to Dacca.
events.significance: The transit sequence is recorded in the disciples’ biography.

events.title: Dacca: teaching and pilgrimage
events.description: He travelled with disciples and arranged a pilgrimage with his mother. In Dacca he spoke at Jagannath College and near Pogose School.
events.significance: The final public tour joined family duty with continued teaching.
events.people: Bhuvaneshwari Devi; disciples and local hosts

events.title: Pilgrimage with his mother
events.description: He went by boat to Langalbandh with his mother’s party for the Budhashtami bathing festival.
events.significance: The journey helped fulfil a cherished wish of his mother.

events.title: At Nag Mahashaya’s home
events.description: He visited the home of the late devotee Nag Mahashaya and was received by his wife.
events.significance: The visit honoured an exemplary householder devotee of Sri Ramakrishna.

events.title: Pilgrimage to Chandranath
events.description: He visited the sacred site of Chandranath near Chittagong during the eastern journey.
events.significance: The pilgrimage extended beyond Dacca into the region now in southeastern Bangladesh.

events.title: A stay at Goalpara
events.description: Goalpara is recorded among his stops on the journey through Assam.
events.significance: It forms part of the documented eastern itinerary.

events.title: Gauhati and Kamakhya
events.description: He visited Kamakhya and gave lectures in Gauhati while his health was declining.
events.significance: The journey included one of the region’s major Shakti pilgrimage sites.

events.title: Shillong and Henry Cotton
events.description: He stayed at Shillong in hopes of better health, met Chief Commissioner Sir Henry Cotton and gave a lecture.
events.significance: The stay was part of his last public tour.

events.title: Life at the Math
events.description: After returning in May, he spent much of his time at Belur, teaching privately, writing and attending to the community despite serious illness.
events.significance: The last phase of his work focused increasingly on the training of others.

events.title: Durga Puja at Belur
events.description: The Math celebrated Durga Puja in the image, with Sri Sarada Devi present in the nearby garden house. Vivekananda took part as health allowed.
events.significance: The celebration brought worship, community and feeding of the poor together.

events.title: A visit to Kalighat
events.description: At his mother’s request, he fulfilled a vow connected with a childhood illness by worshipping at Kalighat.
events.significance: The visit reflected both filial devotion and his continued reverence for the Divine Mother.
events.uncertainty: The city marker is used; no exact day is established.

sources.locator: Site 2: Swami Vivekananda’s worship at Kalighat; no exact visit day given

events.title: The last pilgrimage to Buddha Gaya
events.description: He returned to Buddha Gaya with Japanese visitors, including Okakura Kakuzō, and was received by the Mahant.
events.significance: The last journey revisited a place from the early years of his discipleship.
events.uncertainty: A birthday is mentioned in the biography; this does not securely identify the Gregorian day because birth anniversaries also followed the religious calendar.

events.title: A final stay in Varanasi
events.description: He stayed in Varanasi, met scholars and supported young people serving sick and destitute pilgrims.
events.significance: Their work developed into the Ramakrishna Mission Home of Service.

events.title: Teaching to the end
events.description: He returned to Belur and continued classes and conversations with monks and visitors as his health permitted.
events.significance: Training the next generation remained central to his final months.

events.title: A final meeting with Nivedita
events.description: The biographical account records a meal he served to Sister Nivedita during a visit shortly before his passing.
events.significance: The remembered act of personal service became especially poignant to his disciple.

events.title: Mahasamadhi at Belur Math
events.description: After a day that included meditation, a Sanskrit class and a walk with Swami Premananda, he retired to his room and passed away that evening.
events.significance: The Order remembers his passing as Mahasamadhi. He was 39 years old.
events.uncertainty: Mahasamadhi is the devotional term used by the Order. No unverified medical cause or prediction is supplied.
